# Find what made the 100k Matrix pane content-sized before the tab crash

## Context

Found in manual testing of `apps/workstation` on `dev` (2026-10-22). After a few layout steps, the 100k Matrix pane ran past the window's right edge. The App worker logged an endless `[Row, Row]` duplicate-id loop, and Chrome climbed to about 160 % CPU before the tab crashed ("Aw, Snap!").

#19991 fixed the two engine defects behind the crash (#19998, merged):
- an unbounded view measured the body's full 5,000,050 px scroll height, so `createRowPool` built 99,970 rows;
- `items.push(...newRows)` threw a `RangeError` after every row had registered its id.

It left the **trigger** out of scope: what made the Matrix pane's chain content-sized in the first place. With #19998 in, a forced content-sized pane no longer hangs the worker. The trigger itself is still unexplained.

## Known so far

- **The three committed steps** ("Undo 3") are encoded in the layout restored after the crash: Live Event Stream dropped on the bottom root edge (`split-root-0`), Evidence Audit split before it (`split-tabs-feed-0-0`), and Resident Activity Timeline moved into that pane (`tabs-audit-0`).
- **The operator's account:** "moving a grid was certainly involved". That was most likely a fourth action, which never committed because the worker wedged mid-drop.
- **Headless replays on `dev` stayed healthy** at the operator's 1278×1017 window. In every one the worker answered, no duplicate ids appeared, and the Matrix pane stayed inside the dock host:
  - the restored document applied in one shot;
  - the three operations as three separate Group commits;
  - a real-pointer drag of the Matrix tab across six waypoints, pinging the worker during the drag.

  Headless pointer drops into nested split zones were unreliable, so not every real-gesture variant ran.
- **Hypothesis from the operator:** it is related to the OffscreenCanvas cells. Every Matrix row carries a "Living signal" sparkline, an OffscreenCanvas cell registered in the Canvas worker, so 99,970 rows mean as many canvas registrations. A known latent hazard (#19110): handing an already-transferred canvas over again makes `transferControlToOffscreen` throw silently, and the duplicate-id loop re-created rows whose canvases were already registered. It is open whether the canvas cells are only the amplifier of the crash or also part of its trigger.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/Body.mjs`: `createRowPool()` and the row ids (`getRowId`).
- The sparkline cells: `src/component/Sparkline.mjs` (App worker) and `src/canvas/Sparkline.mjs` (the Canvas worker renderer). The OffscreenCanvas handover goes through `Neo.main.DomAccess`.
- The dock projection that sizes the pane chain during a drag and drop.

## Investigation

1. A live repro with the operator, recording the screen, while the session is read over the Neural Link, read-only. Capture the History rows, the pane chain's computed sizes, and the Canvas worker's registration count before the worker goes deaf.
2. If it reproduces, bisect the pane chain to the first ancestor that loses its definite size, and the operation that made it lose it.
3. Measure the canvas-cell side directly: registrations per created row, and whether a re-created row re-transfers its canvas.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The trigger is identified with a reproduction (steps, conditions, the losing ancestor). Or, if it cannot be reproduced, the ticket closes with the evidence of what was tried.
- [ ] A defect found on the way gets its own fix ticket with a red-on-base e2e, whether in the dock projection or the canvas-cell lifecycle.
- [ ] The canvas-cell hypothesis is confirmed or ruled out with a measurement: registrations per row, and the re-transfer path.

## Out of Scope

- The engine defects #19991 fixed: the unbounded view and the `RangeError` on the spread push.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-10-22T23:04:52Z

**Step 3 measured: one canvas per pooled row node, the nodes move with the pool, and nothing is re-transferred.** (AC-3 evidence; the trigger, AC-1, stays open for the live repro.)

> Corrected 23:2xZ after the operator's challenge: the first version of this comment said "per rendered row" and spoke of "re-created rows", which reads as if the grid created row nodes as it goes. It does not, and the probe below now shows it: "row" here means one of the grid's pooled row nodes, 32 for a 100,000-record store, and they are the same DOM nodes from the first record to the twenty-thousandth.

Setup: headless Chrome through the Neural Link fixture on `dev` b0af996452 (#19998 included), viewport 1278×1017. `src/main/DomAccess.mjs` routed in flight to count every `transferControlToOffscreen` call per node id in `transferCanvasToWorker` and every catch; row and canvas nodes tagged at baseline so a later read can tell a surviving node from a new one. No tracked file touched.

**Recycling (the moving-nodes contract):** `.neo-grid-view` scrolled in ten jumps of 100,000 px (2,000 rows each) across the store, 400 ms settle per jump.

| Jump | First record | Row nodes (same / new) | Canvas nodes (same / new) | Transfers (cumulative) | Failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1 | 32 | 32 | 37 | 0 |
| 1 | 2,017 | 32 / 0 | 32 / 0 | 37 | 0 |
| 5 | 10,017 | 32 / 0 | 32 / 0 | 37 | 0 |
| 10 | 20,001 | 32 / 0 | 32 / 0 | 37 | 0 |

Every intermediate jump reads the same. The row id set (`neo-grid-body-1__row-0` … `__row-31`) is identical before and after; the console stays clean. The five transfers beyond the 32 are the other panes' sparklines.

**Pool growth and shrink (the #19991 recipe):** forcing the pane chain content-sized (`height: auto; flex: none` on the flex container, the tab body and the tab container) pushed the pane to 1082×1017 and grew the pool to 39 nodes; the seven new nodes transferred seven canvases once; restoring the chain shrank the pool back to 32 (`Body#createRowPool` destroys on shrink) and transferred nothing. Through all of it the App worker answered in 1–2 ms and no node was handed over twice.

Reading. The canvas cells keep the grid's node-reuse contract: a pooled row's sparkline is transferred once and then moves across records with its row. The re-transfer hazard (#19110) has no path here. Before #19998 the amplifier was the pool size itself, 99,970 nodes times one canvas each; that is bounded now.

What this does not settle: what made the chain content-sized in the operator's session. Next, in the morning: the live repro with the operator over the Neural Link, read-only, with `get_dom_rect` / `get_computed_styles` polled on the Matrix pane's ancestors during the fourth action ("moving a grid"), to catch the first ancestor whose height stops being definite.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-10-23T12:33:44Z

**Measurements on the candidate e2f77dd0fb (Vega, 2026-10-23 12:2x–12:3xZ), and the plan for the live repro.** #20009 is a v13.3.1 blocker by the operator's ruling (every known grid, dock and Workstation bug blocks), so the row empties either with the trigger named and fixed, or with the ticket closed on the evidence of what was tried (AC-1's second clause).

**What reproduces the symptom's shape.** Forcing the Matrix chain content-sized in both axes up to and including its split (`flex: none; height: auto; width: auto` inline on `.workstation-scale-pane`, its tab body, its tab container and `neo-container-6`, the #19991 recipe widened to the split) at a 1440×900 window: the grid and its body lay out at **1082×900** (bottom 1057 against a host ending at 791) and the split at **1227 wide with its right edge at 1460**, past the 1440 window, clipped by the parent split's `overflow: hidden`. That is the picture from the 10-22 session: the Matrix past the window's right edge and a content-sized chain the grid then measured. The 1082 is the grid's own content width (its column total), the 900 its content height capped by #19998.

**What does not reproduce it.** Shrinking the window to 760 px wide: the whole chain shrinks with the host (3 of 3), so a flex item's `min-width: auto` is not the trigger on its own, and a stylesheet floor (`min-*: 0` / `max-*: 100%` on splits and their children) changes nothing I can show red; I built, measured and reverted it rather than ship a guess.

**What the live session showed.** Over the Neural Link on the operator's Workstation (session `18b4ebca`, before his reload): the Matrix tab container computed `flex: 0.6 1 0%`, `min-height: 0`, `min-width: 0`, `overflow: visible`; its two enclosing splits (`neo-container-6`, `neo-container-3`) computed `flex: 1 1 0%`, `overflow: hidden`, and **`min-height: auto`, `min-width: auto`**, although `LayoutAdapter#projectSplitNode` writes `style: {minHeight: 0, minWidth: 0}` for every projected child, splits included. The style lands on tab containers and not on split elements. Filed as a defect-note; not shown to be the trigger.

**Where the inference points.** Since inline sizing wins over any stylesheet, the forced state can only arise from the engine writing or dropping the chain's inline `flex`/size during an operation. The retained-node paths are the candidates: `Reconciler#moveRetainedTabChrome` sets a retained tab container's `wrapperStyle.flex` to `plan.config.flex ?? null`, and the geometry pass re-applies `flex` only for nodes whose next projection carries one; a retained member whose plan carries no `flex` falls to `flex: 0 1 auto`, content-sized in the split's axis. Not yet caught in the act.

**The live repro (the ticket's step 1), with the operator at the keyboard, me read-only over the Neural Link:** baseline rects and computed `flex`/`min-*` of the chain, then after each of the restored layout's three steps (Live Event Stream → bottom root edge; Evidence Audit split before it; Resident Activity Timeline → that pane), then after the fourth action, moving the Matrix tab, with `get_instance_properties` of the chain's `flex` / `wrapperStyle` read at each step so a nulled inline flex shows as it happens. The first ancestor whose computed `flex` or size stops being definite is the losing member and the operation that did it is the trigger.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-11-06T12:59:56Z

### Closing under AC-1's second clause (2026-11-06)

The trigger did not reproduce, so the ticket closes with the evidence of what was tried, as AC-1 provides. `13.3.1` shipped with this ticket open, so the release-blocker ruling no longer applies.

- **AC-1:** every headless replay on `dev` after #19998 stayed healthy at the operator's 1278×1017 window (body, "Known so far"). Forcing the pane chain content-sized reproduces the symptom's *shape*, with the Matrix past the window's right edge, but no operation was found that produces it. A 760 px window shrinks the whole chain with the host (3 of 3). Measurements: [comment 6364973360](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20009#issuecomment-6364973360). The live Neural Link repro with the operator (Investigation step 1) has not happened in the two weeks since.
- **AC-2:** no defect surfaced on the way. The two engine defects behind the crash were #19991's, fixed by #19998.
- **AC-3:** measured: one canvas per pooled row node, and zero re-transfers across scrolling and pool growth or shrink ([comment 6353261642](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20009#issuecomment-6353261642)).

**If it recurs.** Since #19998, a content-sized pane no longer wedges the worker, so the next sighting can be inspected live. Run `get_dock_topology` and `get_computed_styles` on the pane chain at that moment: the first ancestor without a definite size is the losing one. File a recurrence as a new ticket with that read attached.
